about: Things that happen around this family, for the hackathon day (Saturday 21 November 2026). Each signal says which moment it is (market, rule, life or decision), whether it is simulated (invented for the exercise) or comes from the family's plan or an official source, what it touches in this family's plan, and where in the case data to look. Simulated events are not real news. Amounts are US dollars.

signals.headline: AI chip stocks sell off: Nvidia down 30% in two weeks
signals.what_happened: Simulated. Nvidia has fallen 30% in two weeks. Since 6 November the Nasdaq 100 is down 12% and the S&P 500 is down 8%. Commentators ask whether the AI bubble is bursting.
touches_this_family: Technology is 33.0% of Michael's stock holdings, mostly through VTI.

Closest past shock in the data: when the Liberation Day tariffs were announced (2 Apr 2025) this portfolio fell 8.4%, against 8.2% for a simple mix with the same stock share. A fall that size today would be about $14,500 on $172,000 of investments and cash.
Worst fall in the last three years: 10.2%, recovered in 62 days.
Longer history: in the Global Financial Crisis (Oct 2007 to Mar 2009) the current mix would have lost 19.2% and the recommended mix 11.1%; in the COVID crash (Feb to Mar 2020) 13.2% and 13.1%.
His $113,300 down payment is due in January 2027 and his accessible cash is $30,000, so most of it would come from investments that are falling now (persona O2).
$35,000 of RSUs from his employer sit outside the portfolio and add to the same risk (persona O8).

signals.headline: 2027 tax values published: standard deduction, brackets, child tax credit, Social Security wage base
signals.what_happened: The IRS published the 2027 inflation adjustments on 5 November 2026: standard deduction $16,600 single and $33,200 married filing jointly (from $16,100 and $32,200), brackets indexed, child tax credit $2,300 per child (from $2,200). The Social Security wage base rises to $192,300 for 2027 (from $184,500). They apply from 1 January 2027.
touches_this_family: Single filer: standard deduction rises by $500, from $16,100 to $16,600.
His $180,000 salary is below both wage bases, so the Social Security change does not raise his payroll tax.
No children, so the child tax credit does not apply.
where_in_the_data: legal-values.json (same file as legal/legal-dataset-sample.json): StandardDeductionByYear, FederalIncomeTaxBracketsByYear, ChildTaxCreditByYear, SSWageBaseByYear
sources: SSA contribution and benefit base 2027: $192,300 (https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html; 2027 COLA fact sheet https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/cola/factsheets/2027.html)

signals.headline: Home purchase in January 2027, about six weeks away
signals.what_happened: From the plan. Michael plans to buy a $550,000 home ($566,500 at purchase) with a $113,300 down payment and a 30-year loan of $453,200 at 7%. The monthly payment is $3,015.15, against $2,800 of rent today. Investable assets fall from $178,717 in 2026 to $81,172 in 2027 in the projection.
touches_this_family: Cash covers about 3.2 months of expenses today and 0 months after the January 2027 goals (persona O2).
His score is 26 out of 100; the home changes housing cost, cash, debt and retirement saving at once (persona D3, transition alerts).
Decision style: collaborator, engaged and still seeking advice (persona D5).

signals.headline: Michael posts a promotion on LinkedIn
signals.what_happened: Simulated. Michael announced a promotion to senior manager on LinkedIn. The new salary is not stated. His employer is not named in the data.
touches_this_family: Net cash flow is -$8,336 a year today (persona O5): a raise could close it, or go to lifestyle.
He defers $17,000 to the 401(k) against a $24,500 limit, so $7,500 more is possible (persona O7).
Salary and RSUs from one employer are a concentration already flagged (persona O8).
